title: Open section-component locus in a flat geometrically reduced family
statement: Let (g:P\to T) be flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and of finite presentation (locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated) [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let (sigma:T\to P) be a section of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Assume every fibre of (g) is geometrically reduced [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Let (C\subseteq P) be the union, over (t\in T), of the connected component [def-weil-connected-scheme] of (sigma(t)) in (P_t) [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Then (C) is open [def-weil-open-immersion] in (P).

source.place: Tag 055R, label lemma-connected-along-section-open; proof via Tag 055Q and Tag 055P

proof.text: By Tag 055P, the relative section component locus is locally constructible for every locally finitely presented, quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism with a section. The given flatness and geometrically reduced fibre hypotheses are additional hypotheses, so this applies to the set C in the statement.

By Tag 055Q, the relative section component locus for a flat finitely presented morphism with geometrically reduced fibres is stable under generalization: if p specializes to q and q lies in the component through the section in its fibre, then p lies in the corresponding component. This is exactly the generalization-stability statement recorded in lem-trf-flat-reduced-section-component-generalization.

Fix x in C. Choose an affine open U of P containing x by lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis, and put E=C intersect U. The local constructibility from step 1 restricts to U: intersect each constructible neighbourhood V with U. A retrocompact open in V stays retrocompact in V intersect U, since any quasi-compact open W of V intersect U is also a quasi-compact open of V. Thus the finite Boolean expressions defining constructibility restrict, so E is locally constructible in U. The affine scheme U is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs; lem-trf-locally-constructible-qcqs-global now makes E constructible in U. The generalization stability from step 2 restricts to U, since a specialization between points of U is a specialization in P. Under an affine identification U = Spec A, constructibility and this specialization relation are unchanged (homeomorphisms preserve opens, quasi-compactness and closure). Apply lem-trf-spectrum-constructible-generalization-open to conclude that E is open in U.

source.place: Tag 00I0(2), applied on affine charts to the locally constructible locus from Tag 055P and the generalization property from Tag 055Q

proof.text: For each x in C, step 3 supplies E=C intersect U containing x, open in U. Since U is open in P, E is open in P by the subspace topology. These sets E are contained in C and cover C. Their union is C, so C is open in P.
